# libhamlib-utils

**The command-line tools for hamlib — test a radio before blaming software**

- **Version recorded:** 4.6.2
- **Categories:** `rig-control`
- **Upstream:** <http://www.hamlib.org>

## What it does

Carries `rigctl` and `rigctld`, the command-line and daemon interfaces to hamlib, plus `rotctl` and `rotctld` for antenna rotators. `rigctl` sets and reads frequency, mode, PTT and everything else a backend supports; `rigctld` serves the same over a network socket so several programs can share one radio.

## Why you would want it

`rigctl` is the diagnostic that separates a radio problem from a program problem. When fldigi will not key the transmitter, the question is whether hamlib can, and one command answers it. Nearly every Linux ham program uses hamlib underneath, so a fault reproduced here is a fault in the layer everything shares.

## Before it will work

A CAT interface and access to its serial device -- the `dialout` group. Knowing your radio's hamlib model number, which `rigctl -l` lists.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profiles:** [`satellite`](../profiles/satellite.md), [`station`](../profiles/station.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install libhamlib-utils --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Commands it leaves on your PATH: `rigctl-dummy`.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `libhamlib-utils`

## Known problems

The model number matters and the closest-looking one is often wrong; a mismatched backend produces partial control, where frequency works and mode does not, which reads as a broken cable. Baud rate and, for Icom, the CI-V address must match the radio's own menu settings. `rigctld` and a program opening the serial port directly will fight over it, and the symptom is erratic behaviour rather than an error -- decide which one owns the port.
